remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. At Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature [note missing backing inscription 1] '59th Street Studio 1919.' See gallery photograph 2–a." Abiquiú Notebooks notes backing inscriptions 1, 4. Pictured in 1923 New York (Anderson) Stieglitz installation photograph, see Appendix III, figure 13. Sunami refers to one of several photographers who made photographs of O'Keeffe paintings. Subject refers to the studio of Elizabeth Stieglitz (niece of Stieglitz) at 114 East 59th Street, where O'Keeffe and Stieglitz lived after O'Keeffe's move to New York in 1918. O'Keeffe wrote: "The studio was bright with a north skylight and two south windows. . . . The room back of the studio had a rather narrow window opening into a small court so it was not very light. The painting is what one saw as one looked from the bright room into the darker room" (*Georgia O'Keeffe* [1976], unpaginated, text accompanying entry 16). (Source: Lynes, 1999)
